item.title: Around 3.7 million jobs are directly at risk in Europe's struggling industry, report says
item.description: McKinsey estimates that about 3.7 million jobs are directly at risk in Europe, as almost half of the region's industrial companies were under financial stress or in distress in 2025. Early 2026 data suggest the decline is speeding up, but McKinsey says the problems can be fixed.

item.title: Judi Dench gives her verdict on Robert Pattinson as new James Bond – with one sad reservation
item.description: Oscar-winning actress Dame Judi Dench, who starred alongside Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig in the Bond franchise, shares her thoughts on Robert Pattinson as the new 007 – but says her eye condition may prevent her from watching...

item.title: Czech Republic ready to support Poland after Russian airspace violations
item.description: Prague's offer comes after Russian weapons entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on western Ukraine on 20 November.

item.title: Meet TeoTronico: The sassy, 53-fingered robot pianist challenging human musicians
item.description: In Italy, TeoTronico, a 53-fingered AI powered robotic virtuoso, is challenging the ideas of perfection and what it really means to make music.

item.title: From taxis to trains: Where in Europe can you book rail travel through Uber?
item.description: For domestic rail journeys and cross-border train links, Uber users in France, the UK and Spain can now book tickets through its app.

item.title: ‘Historic victory’: Caged farm animals could be banned in the EU after landmark court ruling
item.description: The case was brought by a citizen-led campaign that gathered nearly 1.4 million signatures from Europeans calling for an end to caged farming.

item.title: Exclusive: Serbia needs more time to define its direction, Student List MP tells Euronews
item.description: Sara el Sarag, representative of the Students' List, discussed Serbia's European integration, its foreign policy priorities, relations with Russia and the Kosovo issue, as Serbia's new political leadership faces growing expectations to clarify its position on the country's European future.

item.title: Biographer: Pope Francis saw visions of devil as warnings
item.description: The late Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times during his lifetime, in extracts from his private diary quoted in a new book.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 25th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 25th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: German hiker battles fierce winds on Torres del Paine suspension bridge
item.description: Violent gusts of wind set a suspension bridge swaying in Chile's Torres del Paine National Park. A fellow hiker captures the moment the German tourist struggled to keep his balance.

item.title: Aid cuts leave 446,000 fewer people on HIV prevention drugs, UN agency warns
item.description: Last year’s global health cuts are reversing the world's progress on HIV, UNAIDS said in a new report.

item.title: Burgas and Huesca-Pirineos among the world’s most innovative airports of 2026
item.description: The Bulgarian airport near the Black Sea was praised for its open-air Gate Garden, which was introduced to handle additional passengers during the busy summer months.

item.title: French navy seizes 3.3 tonnes of methamphetamine from stateless tanker in Pacific
item.description: A boarding team moved in after weeks of surveillance, backed by a helicopter, a Falcon 50 jet and a US Coast Guard patrol plane.

item.title: Tax expert: Planned EU-wide digital tax will damage economy
item.description: EU leaders are meeting this week to discuss the bloc’s next seven-year budget, but governments are divided on how to pay for it.

item.title: European Parliament 'absolutely right' to ensure safeguards against tariffs, says Renew MEP
item.description:
Barry Andrews, an MEP from the Renew group, speaks to Stefan Grobe on the recent trading tariff arrangements with the US.
The US administration has recently floated the idea of resurrecting tariffs against the EU, after their Supreme Court ruled the prior "Liberation Day" tariff scheme unlawful.

item.title: Trump pardons Thanksgiving turkeys Freedom and Feathers
item.description: Donald Trump pardons Thanksgiving turkeys Freedom and Feathers at the White House.

item.title: Serbia's no-show at EU-Western Balkan summit postpones foreign policy test
item.description: Serbia's new Student List leadership will skip Wednesday's EU-Western Balkans summit in Brussels and is not expected to sign its declaration, delaying clarity on whether Belgrade will align with EU foreign policy. Russia sanctions and Kosovo are the main sticking points.

item.title: Farmers' lobbies 'blocking progress' in ending animal cages, says MEP
item.description: Niels Fuglsang, Danish Socialists & Democrats MEP, believes democratic accountability is at "stake" ahead of European Court of Justice ruling over possible delays in the proposal of phasing out cages for animals.

item.title: ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ final trailer breaks records to become second most viewed of all time
item.description: The final trailer for 'Avengers: Doomsday' becomes the second most-viewed of all time, while the film's director has spoken out on Patrick Stewart's last day on set. Stewart died in October aged 86. His appearance as Professor X in the forthcoming Marvel film marks his last screen performance.

item.title: Social Democrat MEP: Faster EU enlargement key to countering Russian influence
item.description: EU and Western Balkan leaders are meeting in Brussels today to revive stalled efforts to bring the region into the bloc.

item.title: Peter Magyar and Volodymyr Zelenskyy open new chapter in Ukraine-Hungary relations
item.description: The Hungarian prime minister and the Ukrainian president met in Transcarpathia. Both called the talks substantive, and said they open a new chapter in relations between the two countries.

item.title: US tells citizens to leave Iran, warns hostilities could escalate fast
item.description: The US Virtual Embassy in Iran said Tehran, Yemen's Houthis and other aligned groups may target US interests and citizens in the region, including companies and institutions. The alert followed Iranian attacks on US assets in Bahrain and Kuwait and a Houthi strike on Riyadh that injured 11 people.

item.title: British households' energy bills to rise to 70% above EU average as energy price cap rises 26%
item.description: Talks to give Britain access to the EU's electricity market are under way, but Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands are among those insisting London pays in first.

item.title: Watch: 'Beaver Supermoon' lights up skies around the world
item.description: The November Beaver Supermoon rises over Rome and Dubai, illuminating the historic Italian capital and the UAE’s modern skyline.

item.title: Moment China launches Shenzhou-24 mission with Pakistani astronaut aboard
item.description: A Chinese rocket carrying three astronauts, including a Pakistani crew member, blasts off for the Tiangong space station on the Shenzhou-24 mission.

item.title: 13 restaurants topped LaListe’s ranking for 2027 – including seven in Europe
item.description: L’Assiette Champenoise in Tinqueux, France, earned a 99.5 score, reserved for the best restaurants in the world, for the first time this year.

item.title: Stunning Supermoon photos: The best shots of last night's Beaver moon lighting up the night sky
item.description: From Germany to Dubai, catch up on the best photos of last night's Supermoon.

item.title: Belgium opens Europe's largest satellite factory in Charleroi
item.description: The factory will start production of European satellite constellation Iris2 project, which aims to rival Starlink, by the end of 2028.

item.title: Protesters rally outside European Parliament against pesticide bill
item.description: Several hundred people gathered outside the European Parliament in Strasbourg to protest against a controversial bill that could allow unlimited authorisations for certain pesticides.

item.title: From childhood memories to art: Inside Ramakech, Morocco's wildly imaginative sculpture park
item.description: From upside-down houses to furniture built for giants, Jean-François Fourtou's sculpture park in the Moroccan city of Marrakech turns childhood memories into a surreal, immersive experience.

item.title: BYD plans car production in France to boost its push into the European market
item.description: BYD has entered exclusive talks to buy Ineos Automotive's Hambach plant in Moselle. The deal could let the top electric carmaker build in France and boost its European presence.

item.title: EU data centres: Tripling capacity, but climate and worker laws lag behind
item.description: The European Commission wants to triple EU data centre capacity for AI and cloud computing within five to seven years, but the rules to measure their environmental impact and protect construction workers are still being written. Watch the video!

item.title: Balkan to the future: The long and winding road to Brussels
item.description: Good morning. Leo Cendrowicz here with your Wednesday newsletter. Today, we’re looking at the Western Balkans’ long road to EU membership, a Danish dilemma for Europe’s Socialists – and, courtesy of the late Pope Francis, a few encounters with the devil himself.

item.title: Europe Today: Montenegro’s president sets out plan for EU membership
item.description: EU and Western Balkans leaders are meeting in Brussels today to discuss enlargement, regional cooperation and how to strengthen security and defence.

item.title: Europeans are turning to heat pumps ahead of a cold winter. But what do they cost to install?
item.description: Almost one in three Europeans say they cannot afford the upfront cost of installing a heat pump.

item.title: Spain's economy is booming. Why are real wages still below their 2009 peak?
item.description: Spain's economy is forecast to grow more than twice as fast as the eurozone's this year, but average pay still buys less than it did in 2009. Rising housing and food costs are putting household budgets under pressure ahead of Sunday's election.

item.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian forces storm Cartagena supermarket
item.description: A botched attempt to rob an armoured vehicle set off the day-long standoff, during which negotiators had already secured the release of 10 captives.

item.title: Teachers clash with police during nationwide strike over education cuts in Chile
item.description: Thousands of teachers marched in Santiago during a nationwide strike against proposed budget cuts to public and higher education, with some protesters clashing with police.

item.title: Europe’s most popular cities for Christmas getaways – according to search trends
item.description: Thinking about a European festive city break this Christmas and New Year? The latest research from TUI Musement has revealed the destinations travellers are searching for the most, with London, Paris and Edinburgh leading the way.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 25th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 25th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Average full-time salaries in Europe: Which countries pay the most and the least?
item.description: Luxembourg's average full-time salary was more than five times Bulgaria's in 2025. Once local prices are taken into account, Greece ranks last, and Luxembourg's average salary buys about three times as much.

item.title: Migrants rescued off Spain's El Hierro as Atlantic crossings continue
item.description: Spanish maritime rescuers have assisted migrants arriving by boat at La Restinga, on the Canary Island of El Hierro. The island has declared a state of emergency after a sharp increase in arrivals from West Africa put pressure on local reception and healthcare services.

item.title: Nicolas Sarkozy to face 2027 Paris trial over alleged paid retraction by witness
item.description: Alongside his wife Carla Bruni, the ex-French president will face court in late 2027, accused of conspiracy and hiding witness tampering over alleged Libyan funding of his 2007 campaign.

item.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to its space station as Pakistani joins Shenzhou 24 crew
item.description: The crew will carry out more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests. according to China's state media reports.

item.title: Summer vitamin D levels may say more about your health than winter levels, study finds
item.description: A Swedish research team set out to identify who could benefit most from taking vitamin D supplements.

item.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat and orders Bern's new Pyongyang office to close
item.description: Switzerland opened the office on 19 October, when Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis travelled to Pyongyang and met senior officials, including his counterpart Choe Son Hui.

item.title: Tech giant Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
item.description: In a statement, Huawei said the acquittal on the racketeering charge "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years."

item.title: Europe Tonight debriefs: can the EU budget compete with China and the US?
item.description: Euronews' daily evening show Europe Tonight welcomed Lukas Gutenberg, director of the Europe Programme at the Bertelsmann Stiftung, to discuss issues such as how the EU plans to do more with less, as well as the latest proposal put forward by Antonio Costa, which foresees another round of big cuts.

item.title: 'It's simply cheaper to fund Ukraine': Ukrainian economist warns Europe against cutting aid to Kyiv
item.description: Cutting financial support for Kyiv risks emboldening Moscow and exposing Europe to further Russian aggression, Tymofiy Mylovanov told Euronews. He warned that forcing Ukraine into concessions without credible security guarantees could pave the way for another war.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Europe faces tough budget negotiations
item.description: To debrief on the EU's passing of its budget, our correspondent Maria Tadeo spoke to Slovak MEP for Progressive Slovakia within the Renew Europe group Lucia Yar on Euronews' new weekly evening show Europe Tonight.
